column3: NASB supplies “who.”
NASB spells “Eloth”; “lay down” is rendered “slept.”
NASB reads “Jechiliah,” the name read aloud, for the written “Jecoliah.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Skilled in the seeing of God” is rendered “had understanding through the vision of God”; the meaning of this phrase is uncertain.
“Made a breach in” is rendered “broke down”; NASB supplies “the area of.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“His name went” is rendered “his fame extended,” and “the entrance of Egypt” as “the border of Egypt.” “Displayed strength upward” is rendered “became very strong.”
“Buttress” is rendered “corner buttress.”
“Dug wells” is rendered “hewed cisterns,” and “orchards” as “fertile fields.” NASB supplies “He also had.”
“To troops” is rendered “by divisions,” and “by the hand of” as “prepared by.”
“Heads of the fathers” is rendered “heads of the households.”
“An army of war” is rendered “an elite army.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“War engines of invention of an inventor” is rendered “engines of war invented by skillful men.”
“According to his strengthening” is rendered “when he became strong.”
“Sons of strength” is rendered “valiant men.”
“Took their stand on” is rendered “opposed.” “Not of you for honor” is rendered “will have no honor.”
“Skin disease” is rendered “leprosy,” and “from on to the altar” as “beside the altar.”
“The priest of the head” is rendered “the chief priest,” and “turned to him” as “looked at him.” “Struck” is rendered “smitten.”
“The house of separateness” is rendered “a separate house”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
“Matters” is rendered “acts.”
“Lay down” is rendered “slept.”
